reason: Repair visibly detached pushing hands and over-wide braking arms.
source_policy: Original generated component PNGs remain intact at original resolution and colors. Rendering uses individually reviewed opaque joint anchors and sleeve regions.
changes: The palm has separate wrist and grip anchors. Forearm endpoint follows the actual wrist opening, while grip stays attached to the cart shaft.
Near and far arms are drawn after the torso and cart so the far sleeve is not erased by the torso.
Arm width is constant along the projected opaque source outline. Only the longitudinal direction changes length.
Six upper-sleeve source ends are reviewed independently to exclude duplicate exposed-skin caps.
Pusher and both feet move together 22 logical units farther behind the axle, with ground resampled at their own positions. Speed, route, controls and scoring remain unchanged.
The bridge board's walking edge remains anchored to the same physical road height as the wheel bottom.
Preparation cover now comes from the v7 ordinary-input scene. Repeated cover export follows its source record instead of reverting to the v4 detached-hand image.

evidence.ordinary_input: All six avatar identities reach the end in 23.8416667 seconds, zero recoveries. Includes individual uphill, crest, downhill, braking and bridge captures plus 16 travel motion frames at 50 ms intervals.
evidence.tests: 7 cart-filtered tests passed, 1294 assertions. This targeted run also included existing cart tests selected by the project's GUT configuration.
evidence.image_review: Read six identities at ordinary push and braking, travel uphill/downhill/bridge, and representative travel motion frames. Wrist connection and stable arm width are visible in these captured frames.

limits: Not user art acceptance and not a claim of human-reviewed normal-speed continuous animation. Capture and ordinary-input success do not establish game feel or historical vehicle reconstruction.
user_review: REJECTED: arms longitudinally stretched into bands; anatomical proportions wrong. Joint continuity checks missed the overall silhouette.
superseded_by: v8 intact generated upper-body pose; awaiting user review
